annotations.text:
Active Matters — five ways to show the tiles WITHOUT a card box.
Every option uses the same design-system tokens (Source Serif 4 titles, Public Sans, JetBrains Mono for dates/clients, the neutral + green-status scale). No option uses a surface-plus-border-plus-shadow container, a gradient fill, or a rounded box with a left accent bar. The first tile of each artboard is frozen in its hover state so you can see the interaction; the rest animate in on load. Tell me which to build into the dashboard.

OPTION A — Docket Rules
Hairline-ruled full-width rows; due dates right-aligned in a fixed mono column so they read down like a ledger. Hover lifts the row to solid white and firms its rules — the exact treatment the app already uses on Recent Matters.
Good for: density, a docket / printed-brief register, fitting 8+ at a glance.
Trade-off: status reads quieter than a coloured pill; rows can feel uniform.

OPTION B — Column Rules
3-up grid held together only by thin rules — vertical between columns, horizontal between rows, nothing on the outer edge. Hover thickens the cell's left rule to near-black, tints the cell faintly and nudges its content right.
Good for: keeping the current 3-across shape, a statute / newspaper-column feel.
Trade-off: interior rules at 3 columns can look busy; needs crisp alignment.

OPTION C — Baseline Tabs
Each tile sits on one hairline baseline, like a filled-in form field. Status drops the pill for a small-caps eyebrow. Hover wipes a 2px near-black rule in from the left; the baselines draw themselves L→R on load.
Good for: a light, form-like / index-card register with a satisfying hover.
Trade-off: only a bottom edge — needs generous spacing or it can read unfinished.

OPTION D — Contents Page
No chrome at all. The serif title is the object; status is a single coloured dot ahead of it; a quiet mono line underneath. Grouping is vertical rhythm alone. Hover deepens the title grey→black and slides a serif arrow in; on load each title is unmasked left-to-right.
Good for: maximum restraint, an editorial contents-page feel.
Trade-off: no grouping cue; status is subtle; fewer items fit per screen.

OPTION E — Priority Spine
One vertical spine; every matter is a node on it, dot coloured by urgency, ordered top-down from most pressing to no deadline. Hover swells the node, pushes its connector to near-black and slides the row right. The spine draws downward on load, then nodes drop in.
Good for: making urgency spatial — the eye starts at the top.
Trade-off: implies an order that fights the sort control; single column, so taller.
